import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Aggregate total sales by product and size
# This will give us the sum of 'total' for each unique combination of 'product' and 'size'
product_size_sales = df.groupby(['product', 'size'])['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Determine the order of products on the x-axis based on their overall total sales (descending)
product_order = df.groupby('product')['total'].sum().sort_values(ascending=False).index

# Define a preferred logical order for sizes (e.g., Small, Medium, Large, Extra Large)
# Filter this list to only include sizes actually present in the dataset to avoid errors
size_order_preferred = ['Small', 'Medium', 'Large', 'Extra Large']
unique_sizes_in_data = df['size'].unique()
size_order_filtered = [s for s in size_order_preferred if s in unique_sizes_in_data]

# Create the figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8)) # Set a larger figure size for better readability

# Create a grouped bar chart using seaborn.barplot
# x='product' will be the main categories, hue='size' will create groups within each product
sns.barplot(
    data=product_size_sales,
    x='product',
    y='total',
    hue='size',
    order=product_order,       # Apply the custom order for products
    hue_order=size_order_filtered, # Apply the custom order for sizes in the legend
    palette='viridis'          # Use a perceptually uniform colormap
)

# Add a title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Total Sales by Product and Size', fontsize=18)
plt.xlabel('Product', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=14)

# Rotate x-axis labels to prevent overlap, especially if product names are long
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)

# Place the legend outside the plot area to prevent obscuring the bars
plt.legend(title='Size', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Add a grid for easier reading of values
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure as a high-resolution PNG file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
